C-RECORD-SCHEMA-2-0785BD5E.IntentSummary:
Author the execution for the approved, fingerprinted spec `.ngrace/changes/active/C-RECORD-SCHEMA-2-0785BD5E/spec.xml` (approved `approved` at `437d9bd`, three commits above `main` `aaae414`) and only within it; the plan conforms to the spec, it does not extend, narrow or reinterpret it. The spec's six resolved `Clarifications` (`INV-RECORD-SERIALIZER-PLACEMENT`, `INV-RECORD-BOUNDARY`, `INV-RECORD-SEPARATOR`, `INV-RECORD-HASH`, `INV-RECORD-HEADROOM`, `INV-RECORD-SWEEP-RETIRED`) are the maintainer's rulings and stand as written; every one is implemented here or named a `NonGoal` by the spec.
This plan is re-homed from the archived predecessor draft `.ngrace/changes/archive/C-RECORD-SCHEMA-1-1D8D868F/plan.xml` (the skill's `approved_plan_immutability` path), changing only the id where it is data and the items the successor spec forces: the golden re-capture, the three-entry flush, and the corrected projections.
The task order is the spec's order of operations, one task per stage, and each task's `Verification` is evaluated on the tree that stage leaves (the phase rule): `T-001` lands the shape schema, the canonical serializer (the new `scripts/record-serialize.ts`), the shared-headroom fold **and the golden re-capture** — the serializer and the regenerated goldens must land in one task, because the `:2147` golden relation test is red between them and `T-001`'s own suite command would fail otherwise; `T-002` lands the repository-boundary refusal; `T-003` lands the separator trim at the parse boundary, the one-time sweep and the 56 recomputed `record-inventory.json` hashes; `T-004` performs the one-time flush of `F252`, `D40` and `F265` plus the charter row, then `--rewrite-roots`. The close (`--retire` `moved 6`, the gates, the status write, the archive move) is not a task; it is owned by the authority, and no task performs any part of it.
The `D30` window. It opens when this bundle's execution begins — `T-001` — and stays open until the close: no other dispatch reads or rewrites the record while this bundle does. The flush runs during execution under that window (`T-004`, after the sweep), never at the close; the spec's "at the start of execution" means during execution and before the close. The sweep and the flush are the spec's two hand writes and both run under the open window.
The two hand writes and their vehicle. Both are one-time and neither is committed: a throwaway script that imports the engine's exported `stripBodySeparator`, its canonical serializer and `parseFrozenMarkdown`, is authored under a scratch path outside the tree, and is run once. The precedent read for shape only is `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY-3`'s archived plan (the last flush before this one); it was never transformed. Canonical-at-rest after each hand write — `serialize(parse(file))` byte-equal to `file`, asserted by `T-001`'s shipped test — is the proof that the hand write went through the serializer and not around it. The sweep applies the trim to the four genre files and recomputes exactly the 56 `record-inventory.json` hashes it holds for swept bodies, with a parse-equality proof that only the separator tail moved; the flush writes `F252` and `F265` live into `findings.xml`, `D40` live into `rulings.xml` with no `CodifiedIn`, three `Entry` elements into `decisions.xml`, and the row into `registry.xml`, and it does **not** append to the inventory. The flush's delta equals the element sum exactly — findings +43 (`F252` 20 + `F265` 23), rulings +45 (`D40` 45) — with no non-element line. The row is minted with an empty `<Number>`, a `<Charter>` carrying the successor's searched-before-minting statement (the predecessor `C-RECORD-SCHEMA-1-1D8D868F` is the one prior bundle, its `mint-search` line `1 active, 0 archive`), `<Pays>F207 F221 F235 F252 F265</Pays>`, and a token-free `<StatusText>` with no `Closed with` sentence.
The scopes, stated with their reasons and checked against the shipped predicate. `DurableScope` is `<None />`: the spec's `AffectedAreas` names no module ("No graph module is written or minted … the record files under `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/` are owned by no module in `.ngrace/graph/main.xml`"), and no `M-*` / `DF-*` / `IC-*` appears in the spec's `AffectedAreas`, so the plan's `DurableScope` covers nothing. `ObservedWriteScope` lists exactly the paths the four tasks force: the two engine scripts and their two suites, the new serializer module, `scripts/prove-record-preservation.ts`, the seven record files, `record-inventory.json`, **and the seven golden fixtures under `scripts/fixtures/record-parse/golden/`** (regenerated by `T-001` because the serializer's canonical form differs from their bytes — the spec measured 10 top-level gap anomalies, 5+5). It does **not** list `decisions.md`: the stub is written only by `--split` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:579`), which this bundle never reruns, and the flush writes index entries to `decisions.xml`, not the stub — driven, the stub is unchanged. It does **not** list the predicate inputs `scripts/fixtures/record-parse/input/` (the spec rules them untouched, the committed snapshot materialized verbatim) and does **not** list the bundle's own artifacts (the review skips `spec.xml`, `plan.xml` and `design-context.xml` by identity) and does **not** list `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md` (read, never written). `isModuleOwnableWritePath` is false for every path outside `src/`, and this scope names no `src/` path, so `change.graph-anchors-miss-write-scope` cannot fire.
The mapping, fixed by the spec's own Constraint: exactly one criterion — `AC-NO-CURRENT-MODE` — carries no `CloseEvidence` and is mapped by exactly one task `Satisfies`, carried by `T-001`; it is this plan's only `Satisfies` and no other task carries one. Every other criterion is close-bound by its own `CloseEvidence` and a `Satisfies` of any of them is the shipped error `change.close-evidence-and-satisfied`. `AC-CLOSE-LINT`'s `CloseEvidence` runs `--fail-on warnings`, so an unmapped `AC-NO-CURRENT-MODE` would make the bundle's own close unsatisfiable; it is mapped. No task `Verification` contains a current-mode lint of this root: no command text contains `--assertions current`, and none invokes `ngrace lint` of this root omitting `--assertions`.
The assertions. `BaselineAssertions` pin the standing world with existence pins and the four shipped instruments that are green at the baseline — the record suite (131 pass / 0 fail / 2656 `expect()` call, measured at this plan's commit), the preservation suite (5 pass / 0 fail / 11 `expect()` call), the shipped validator and the preservation validator (each `record-retirement: ok` / `record-preservation: ok`, exit 0). They do **not** pin the 68-body count, a root value, or a `moved N` string — a needle the bundle flips by design belongs in a test or a probe, not a baseline assertion. `TargetAssertions` re-assert the four instruments (they must stay green on the changed engine) and add `MustExist` for the new `scripts/record-serialize.ts`.
The faithful-copy law (`F231`), discharged at plan time on a whole-repository `rsync` copy from `437d9bd` with untracked `.ngrace/changes/` carried, `.git` carried, a real `node_modules`, and `.ngrace/scratch` present; once the refusal exists in a copy, every engine command in that copy runs from inside the copy, because the refusal makes the partial-copy shape loud by design. The driven close on the prototype copy (the engine, with a hand flush and a hand sweep, no serializer and no refusal yet, with the spec's whitespace-stripped-tail trim) reproduced the whole state chain: sweep 68 bodies, roots findings `7434/333/7767` and rulings `1670/213/1883` after `--rewrite-roots`; flush roots findings `7477/290/7767`, rulings `1715/168/1883`, registry `13/13/26`, index `270/26/296`; `--retire` **`moved 6`** then **`moved 0`**; post-close roots findings `7343/372/7715` (the moving-genre clamp lowered the ceiling, never raised it), rulings held `1715/168/1883`, registry `12/14/26`, index `265/31/296`; the five findings retired with `<PaidBy>C-RECORD-SCHEMA-2-0785BD5E</PaidBy>`, the row retired `kind="chartered"`, `D40` live with its index layer live, and the shipped validator green before and after. The engine pieces the plan itself adds (the serializer, the schema enforcement, the refusal) are not drivable at plan time because the tasks below write them; their commands are recorded and are driven green in the executor's tree as the task leaves it, and every red direction the plan names is driven by the task's own test.
The golden fixtures, in scope and regenerated. The successor spec rules the seven files under `scripts/fixtures/record-parse/golden/` into write scope as regenerated because the serializer's canonical form differs from their bytes: the copy drive measured ten top-level gap anomalies — golden `rulings.xml` carries five `Decision`s at four-space indent (`D5.2`, `D6`, `D9.1`, `D19`, `D25`) and golden `rulings-retired.xml` five at column zero (`D24`, `D5.1`, `D7`, `D9`, `D18`) — and the shipped golden relation test ("a fixture `--retire` writes byte-for-byte the files the shipped engine wrote at capture time", `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:2147`) pins those bytes. `T-001` therefore regenerates them: it runs the serializer-routed engine over the untouched predicate inputs (`scripts/fixtures/record-parse/input/`) and writes `golden/`. The red direction of the `:2147` test is the pre-regeneration goldens against the serializer-routed engine (the test fails on the drifted gaps); its green is the re-captured canonical bytes. The re-capture is the pin this bundle flips, and it is why the goldens are in `ObservedWriteScope`.
The close, stated once and never performed by a task. The executor emits its own execution-time cursor events per task inside the open epoch (opened, progress, an attempt with signature kind and key on every failed verification cycle, verification-unavailable when evidence cannot be collected, pause and resume around interruptions) and does not omit them; command-run is produced by the CLI's `--run-commands` path, never hand-invented. The terminal event, the cursor fold, every gate, the status write, the archive move and the close's own record retirement move are close acts owned by the authority. On the faithful post-close copy the house sequence is: commit the approved plan, `gate approve --artifact plan`, baseline `--run-commands`, the T-states with their reds and greens, `--assertions target`, `cursor advance --kind terminal` + `cursor fold`, `lint --assertions final --run-commands`, `review`, `gate verdict --outcome pass`, `gate apply`, `gate archive`, `apply --change C --path .`, `--retire` (`moved 6`) then `--retire` (`moved 0`), post-archive `review`, `gate verdict --outcome pass` (the CloseEvidence evaluator; `Result` and `Exit` per criterion read from the ledger), and `bun run validate:ci`. The byte-invariance baseline for every diff command is the spec's base commit `aaae414ba89c86b1e3e7125943637b453591a9f9`; every diff sees tracked paths only; every archive diff excludes this bundle's own departure and arrival. Every new test that walks the real record or the real archive carries the house per-test timeout `}, 60_000)`. When this plan names a tag or attribute form it writes character data with entities (`<`, `>`, `&`) and never paraphrases the brackets away.

T-001.Title: Land the declared shape schema and the canonical serializer in the new module `scripts/record-serialize.ts`, route every record write through it, fold the rulings headroom onto the retire path's constant, and regenerate the seven byte-pinned golden fixtures against the serializer's canonical output

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The schema, declared and enforced. `scripts/record-serialize.ts` declares the shape of the seven record files as the engine's contract, not a corpus snapshot: per file the expected root (`Findings`, `Rulings`, `Registry`, `RecordIndex`) with the root attribute set present on live roots and absent on retired siblings; the genre element (`Finding` / `Decision` / `Row` / `Entry`); its required attribute set and value forms; its required children and their order (`Finding`: `PaidBy`? `Title` `Body`; `Decision`: `Title` `Body` (`CodifiedIn` | `TaughtIn`)*; `Row`: `Number` `Charter` `Pays` `StatusText` `Successor`?; `Entry`: none, self-closing); the layer-conditional children (`PaidBy` on `Finding` in either layer, required only on the retired layer; `Successor` retired `Row` only; `CodifiedIn`/`TaughtIn` on `Decision` in either layer); and the depth bound. `TaughtIn` (`path`, `section`) is admitted even though the corpus carries zero instances, because the engine reads it (`childNodes(node, "TaughtIn")`). The default validation and all four write modes (`--split`, `--retire`, `--stamp-paid-by`, `--rewrite-roots`) check the schema before any write; a violation refuses (exit non-zero, nothing written). Green: the seven live record files and the seven goldens report zero violations, and the suite's planted violations — a `Finding` nested in a `Finding`, a genre element nested below the root, an unexpected grandchild, a missing required child — each refuse. Red (driven by the task's test): the planted nested `Finding`.

The canonical serializer, on every write, and canonical at rest. `scripts/record-serialize.ts` emits the declared canonical form (two spaces per depth, close tag at the open tag's indent, self-closing empty elements, canonical attribute order per element type, entity escaping of `&` `<` `>` `"`, a trailing newline after the root close tag) and preserves body prose byte-for-byte — only structural whitespace moves. Of the 18 `writeFileSync` call sites in `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts`, the **16 XML writes** route through the serializer; the other two are not XML and cannot: `:456` writes `record-inventory.json` and keeps its fixed JSON form (`JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)` plus a trailing newline), and `:579` writes the `decisions.md` stub and is unreachable (only `--split` writes it, and `--split` refuses a stub — this bundle never reruns it). `scripts/prove-record-preservation.ts` hashes the same bytes. Green: `serialize(parse(serialize(x)))` is byte-equal to `serialize(x)` for the seven golden fixtures and the planted documents; and at every run `serialize(parse(file))` is byte-equal to `file` for all seven live record files (canonical at rest, which is what makes a hand edit outside the serializer visible). Red (driven by the task's test): a planted non-canonical byte in a copied record file reddens the canonical-at-rest walk; the walk locates its target by walking the record, never a file named in advance.

The shared-headroom fold. The split path's dead copy of the rulings headroom formula (`Math.floor(2 * median(...))`, `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:522`) and the retire path's live one (`Math.floor(7 * median(...))`, `:1273`) are replaced by one shared headroom function using the retire path's constant (7x); the split path's copy is removed; and a test asserts both modes derive the same headroom from the same input. Red (driven by the task's test): an input whose two paths would have disagreed under the old constants.

The golden re-capture. The seven files under `scripts/fixtures/record-parse/golden/` are regenerated against the serializer's canonical output by running the serializer-routed engine over the untouched predicate inputs under `scripts/fixtures/record-parse/input/` (the spec rules those inputs un-canonicalized): the fixture builder `scripts/fixtures/record-parse/build-fixture.ts` is used **unchanged** — it only materializes `input/` into the throwaway root and never writes `golden/`, so it is not in `ObservedWriteScope` — invoked with the flags the golden test uses (`--c-selection-row`); the engine's `--retire` then writes the record through the serializer, and the seven emitted bytes are copied back into `golden/`. Green: the shipped golden relation test (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:2147`, "a fixture `--retire` writes byte-for-byte the files the shipped engine wrote at capture time") passes on the re-captured canonical bytes, and `serialize(parse(golden))` is byte-equal to the regenerated golden for each file. Red (driven before the re-capture): the same test against the pre-regeneration goldens fails on the ten drifted top-level gaps — golden `rulings.xml` five `Decision`s at four-space indent (`D5.2`, `D6`, `D9.1`, `D19`, `D25`), golden `rulings-retired.xml` five at column zero (`D24`, `D5.1`, `D7`, `D9`, `D18`). The re-capture is the pin this bundle flips.

T-002.Title: Add the repository-boundary refusal to the engine: a record directory outside the cwd's `.ngrace/`-rooted boundary is refused before any read or write, with a named message, while a whole-repository copy run from inside the copy is accepted

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The refusal, both directions. The engine resolves the repository boundary from the tree — the presence of `.ngrace/` at the cwd, never git — and refuses, before any read or write and with a named message that names the path, the boundary and the faithful-copy remedy, a record directory that resolves outside it. Green (driven by the task's test on isolated roots): a whole-repository copy run from inside the copy is accepted and moves; the shipped validator stays green inside the copy. Red (driven by the task's test): the same record bytes passed as a partial copy from the real root are refused with exit non-zero and no file changed, where the shipped engine reports `moved 0`. The test locates its fixture root by the shipped resolver, never a file named in advance, and carries the house per-test timeout `}, 60_000)` for every case that walks the real archive.

The engine surface stays under `scripts/`; no `src/` file moves for the refusal. The engine and its suite are the only files this task writes; the record is untouched and the goldens (regenerated by `T-001`) are not re-written here.

T-003.Title: Trim the separator at the parse boundary, sweep the 68 existing bodies in one pass, and recompute the 56 record-inventory.json hashes the sweep changes so the preservation proof stays green

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The trim and the invariant walk, defined on the whitespace-stripped tail. `stripBodySeparator` strips trailing whitespace and blank lines from a body's decoded text, then removes a final `---` line and the blank gap before it, and keeps a single trailing newline; it is applied at the parse boundary (`parseFrozenMarkdown`), in the one-time sweep and in the preservation walk, so all three agree on bytes. Green: a flush-invariant walk over every layer of the four genre files — "ends with a separator line" evaluated after the same strip — asserts none carries one. Red (driven by the task's test), the three shapes the walk must catch: a plain `---` as the last line; a `---` followed by a blank line (`rulings.xml`'s `d20`); and the same-line `---</Body>`. The walk locates its target by walking both layers, never a file named in advance.

The one-time hand sweep and the inventory. The sweep removes the separator from all 68 existing bodies (31 live findings, 23 retired findings, 13 live decisions including `d20`, 1 retired decision), measured deltas **137 lines** across the four genre files (findings live 62, findings-retired 46, rulings live 27 — `d20` loses three, the others two — rulings-retired 2), and recomputes the 56 `record-inventory.json` hashes it holds for swept bodies, with a parse-equality proof that only the separator tail moved. The retired siblings are swept and that is a permitted write (the spec's `INV-RECORD-SWEEP-RETIRED`). The inventory is not appended to. The sweep is a throwaway script run once, not committed, importing the engine's exported helper and serializer; canonical-at-rest after the write is the proof it went through the serializer. Green: `prove-record-preservation` exits 0 and the shipped validator is green. Red (driven): without the inventory recompute, the shipped proof reports exactly 56 `missing-body-hash` findings (measured on the prototype copy).

The sweep touches only the four genre files and the inventory; the registry, the index and the stub are untouched; no ceiling is raised (`--rewrite-roots`, run after the sweep, holds ceilings and re-derives `base`).

T-004.Title: Flush the staged F252, D40 and F265 through the serializer, mint the charter row with its five-token Pays, and re-derive the four live roots with --rewrite-roots, leaving the inventory untouched

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The flush. `F252` and `F265` are written live into `findings.xml` (retired later by the close); `D40` is written live into `rulings.xml` with no `CodifiedIn` and no `TaughtIn` (the `D38` manner, "not yet built"); three index `Entry` elements are written into `decisions.xml`, with `genre` and `layer` agreeing with the holding file; the charter row `C-RECORD-SCHEMA-2-0785BD5E` is written into `registry.xml` with an empty `<Number>`, a `<Charter>` carrying the successor's searched-before-minting statement — that the name was searched over `.ngrace/changes/archive/` and both registry layers and the predecessor `C-RECORD-SCHEMA-1-1D8D868F` is the one prior bundle (its `mint-search` line, `1 active, 0 archive`), no other row or directory carrying the name — `<Pays>F207 F221 F235 F252 F265</Pays>` naming exactly those five tokens, and a token-free `<StatusText>` with no `Closed with` sentence. Green: the shipped validator is green and the four live roots satisfy `base + headroom = ceiling` with `base` equal to the shipped metric read back after `--rewrite-roots` (prototype copy: findings `7477/290/7767`, rulings `1715/168/1883`, registry `13/13/26`, index `270/26/296`), the flush's delta equal to the element sum (+43 findings, +45 rulings) with no non-element line. Red (driven by the task's own test, not the validator): an exists-once-across-layers walk for `D40`, `F252`, `F265` and the row `C-RECORD-SCHEMA-2-0785BD5E` fails before the flush — each is zero across both layers — and passes after — each exactly once, layer agreeing. The shipped validator knows nothing of the buffer and is green before the flush, so it is not the red instrument.

The flush is the last sanctioned hand write and leaves the inventory untouched, exactly as every flush since the split has. It is a throwaway script run once, not committed, importing the engine's serializer and `parseFrozenMarkdown`; canonical-at-rest after the write is the proof it went through the serializer. The buffer `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md` is read, never written. The registry and index files it writes are not appended to elsewhere; the stub `decisions.md` is not written.
